The present petition filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. seeks quashing of FIR No. 923/2018,
under Sections 498A/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Binda Pur, New Delhi and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the Court of Ms. Divya Yadav, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dwarka Court, Delhi.
2. Ms. Jaso Devi has been impleaded as petitioner no. 2 and the amended memo of parties has been taken on record.
3. The marriage between petitioner no.1/husband and respondent no.2/wife was solemnized on 30.05.2014.

4. Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2/complainant lodged an FIR on 02.11.2018 against petitioner no. 1(husband) and petitioner no. 2 (mother-in-law).
5.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the parties arrived at amicable settlement vide settlement deed/MOU dated 27.02.2023.
It is further stated that the parties are living together since April 2020.

7. The Complainant/respondent No.2 states that the matter has been settled and she is living with petitioner no. 1 since April 2020 and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed against the petitioners.
8. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

9. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303, Honble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes by observing as under:-
"61.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceedings or continuation of criminal proceedings would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceedings."

10. In view of the aforesaid circumstances, and the fact that the parties have put a quietus to the dispute, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the present FIR No. 923/2018, under Sections 498A/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Binda Pur, New Delhi and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the Court of Ms. Divya Yadav, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dwarka Court, Delhi.

11. In the interest of justice, the petition is allowed, and the FIR No. 923/2018, under Sections 498A/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Binda Pur, New Delhi and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the Court of Ms. Divya Yadav,
learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dwarka Court, Delhi, is hereby quashed.
12. Petition is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
13. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
AMIT SHARMA, J MARCH 22, 2023/ab
